subject: Window seats with integrated storage
hook: From an empty bay to a seat with drawers: here's how it's built.
ig:
From an empty bay to a seat with drawers: here's how it's built.

Window seats look simple, but every one starts with measuring a bay that's rarely square and a sill that's rarely level.

Measure. Width at several heights, depth into the bay, sill height and the radiator below.

Cut. Panels are cut to size on our sliding table panel saw.

Edge. Every visible edge is banded with matching ABS edging.

Drill. The boring machine puts in the holes for drawer runners and fixings so everything lines up.

Assemble. The carcass and drawers are built and checked in the workshop, never sent out flat-packed.

Fit. Our team installs it, scribes it to the walls and adds the seat.

Got a bay that's currently home to a pile of shoes? Comment SEAT and we'll send you the link.
fb:
A quick look at how a window seat comes together in our Hanley workshop.

We measure the bay carefully (they're rarely square), then panels are cut, edged, drilled for the drawer runners and assembled in the workshop. Our own team fits it on site, scribes it to the walls, and on goes the cushion.

If your bay window could be working harder, have a look at our bespoke furniture and get in touch.
